figures.vasca: Dorin Vasca — first president, driven out in the Turn of the Year, presumed alive somewhere in the west. His remnant is a low-grade insurgency risk rather than a closed chapter.
figures.baran: Cyrus Baran — chairman of the State Council through 1992, architect of the handover, and pointedly not a candidate at the Reckoning. He has no formal power and more credibility than anyone who does.
figures.doncic: General Aurel Doncic — commanded the National Guard in the Turn of the Year. Where that authority went afterwards is not a matter of public record.
figures.yeska: Bogdan Yeska — ran the Falcons, and before that a great deal of what crossed the border unofficially. Neither prosecuted nor entirely retired.
figures.radic: Anton Radic — president of the First Republic, 1918–1921. Died in exile. His portrait is back on the wall in the chamber.
figures.draven: Aurel Draven — the philosopher-economist whose theory of collectivised production gave the Union its doctrine and its justification for everything that followed.
figures.sevra: Queen Sevra — the fourteenth-century sovereign under whom the Terzhan Crown reached the whole Kelvet coast. Ardenian and Vetreni classrooms draw opposite conclusions from the same reign.
figures.stanik: Marek Stanik — President of Ardenia, constitutional lawyer and Kestrel Square survivor. Elected without a party and carrying a moral mandate separate from the Chamber's.
figures.lostane: Vera Lostane — Chief Justice of the nine-member Constitutional Court, which may hear a challenge from the President, the government, or thirty members of the Chamber.
figures.grast: Emil Grast — Governor of the National Bank of Ardenia, responsible for a collapsing kron and an independence clause the foreign stabilisation agreement requires him to defend.
figures.meletian_iv: Meletian IV — Catholicos-Patriarch of Vashtera and head of the country's most trusted institution. Consecrated bishop in 1979, he is also one reason opening the Directorate's files is dangerous.
